mainTopic: Buying three trees and the ground between them; selling animal parts; backing out of a sale over a mismatch in the goods
overview: The amud opens by continuing the משנה's rule that someone who buys three trees in another person's field also gets the ground between them. רב אשי asks whether a pit, a water channel, a public road or a row of palms between the trees breaks the group, and these questions stay unanswered (תיקו). רבי tells הלל that a cedar already standing between the trees does not break the group: the buyer gets both the cedar and the ground. רב says the trees may stand in a row, and שמואל says they must form a triangle, like a tripod. רב המנונא challenges שמואל's reason with thorn bushes, and the answer is that only significant plants, real trees, can give ownership of ground. A new משנה then teaches which parts of a slaughtered animal are included when one part is sold, with different rules for large and small animals. It also teaches when a buyer or seller may back out because the goods were better, worse, or a different kind of item than agreed. The גמרא begins with רב חסדא's ruling that if the buyer overpaid and the price later rose, only the buyer may cancel. His reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אשי asks what counts as a break between the trees
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether a pit, a water channel, a public road, or a row of palm trees between the three trees cuts them off from each other. The questions are left unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If there is a pit between the trees, does it separate them? A water channel, does it separate them? A public road, what is the rule? A row of palm trees, what is the rule? The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks four questions about things that might sit between the three purchased trees and split them apart. The גמרא cannot answer, so it says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer gets the ground only if the three trees form one connected group. If something in between breaks that connection, maybe the buyer does not get the ground. Each item is a different kind of break: a hole, flowing water, public land, or other trees.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question he did not know the answer to
A water channel or small stream
Public property, like a public road

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
A pit, does it separate?
phrases.notes: He means a pit lying between the three trees the person bought.

phrases.english: A water channel, does it separate?
A public road, what is the rule?
A row of palm trees, what is the rule?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rule that buying three trees includes the ground between them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a pit, water channel, public road, or row of palms between the trees breaks their connection.

steps.title: הלל asks רבי about a cedar between the trees
steps.stepSummary: הלל asks רבי what happens if a cedar grew between the three trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל asked רבי: If a cedar grew up between them, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: Another question about something between the trees, this time a cedar. The גמרא is about to question how the question was worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cedar is a big, valuable tree. The worry is that it might split the three trees, or might belong to the seller.

phrases.english: Hillel asked Rabbi:
If a cedar grew between them, what is the rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question about what stands between the trees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the rule is for a cedar between the three trees.

steps.title: The גמרא objects that a cedar that grew later is obviously the buyer's
steps.stepSummary: If the cedar grew after the purchase, it grew on the buyer's own land, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Grew"?! It came up in his own property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of הלל's question. If the cedar grew after the sale, the question makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer already owns the ground between the trees. A tree that sprouts later on his ground is clearly his.

phrases.english: "Grew"?!
It came up in his own property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of הלל's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word עָלָה in הלל's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tree that grows after the sale grows on the buyer's own land, so it is obviously his.

steps.title: The question is reworded: a cedar was already there
steps.stepSummary: The real question is about a cedar that already stood between the trees when he bought them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: If there already was a cedar between them, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The question is about a cedar that was there before the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is real. A cedar already standing there might split the trees so the buyer gets no ground, or it might stay with the seller.

phrases.english: Rather: "If there was a cedar between them, what is the rule?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by changing the wording of the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about a cedar that grew after the sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about a cedar that already stood there at the time of sale.

steps.title: רבי answers: he acquires both
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that the buyer acquires the cedar and acquires the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He acquired, and he acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers הלל's question. The cedar does not break the group of trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word קָנָה וְקָנָה means two acquisitions: the cedar and the ground between the trees. So a cedar in the middle does not stop the buyer from getting the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired and he acquired (two things)

phrases.english: He said to him: He acquired, and he acquired.
phrases.notes: Two acquisitions here: he gets the cedar, and he also gets the ground between the trees.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The buyer acquires the cedar and the ground.

steps.title: How must the three trees stand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the three trees must be positioned for the buyer to get the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the shape the three trees must form. It is setting up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about getting the ground may depend on how the trees are arranged in the field.

phrases.english: How must they be standing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what lies between the trees to how the trees are arranged.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The required arrangement of the three trees.

steps.title: רב says a straight line; שמואל says a tripod
steps.stepSummary: רב says the trees may stand in a straight line. שמואל says they must stand in a triangle like a tripod.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: In a row. And שמואל said: Like a tripod.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree about the arrangement of the trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, even three trees in a row are enough. For שמואל, they must form a triangle, like the three legs of a stand for a jug.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a tripod, in a triangle

phrases.english: Rav said: In a row,
and Shmuel said: Like a tripod.
phrases.notes: A three-legged stand, so the trees form a triangle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: כְּשׁוּרָה, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: כַּחֲצוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a straight line is enough. שמואל: only a triangle (tripod).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: the trees may stand in a straight line. שמואל: they must stand in a triangle, like a tripod.

steps.title: Explaining the two views and שמואל's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב would surely agree a triangle works. שמואל rejects a straight line because one can plant seeds between trees in a row.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says a row, all the more so a tripod. The one who says a tripod, but not a row. Why? Because one can sow between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how far each opinion goes and gives שמואל's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A triangle is the stronger case, so רב agrees to it. שמואל says trees in a row leave room to plant crops between them, so the seller did not give up that ground.

phrases.english: The one who says in a row –
all the more so like a tripod;
and the one who says like a tripod –
but in a row, no.
What is the reason?
Because one can sow between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר כְּשׁוּרָה – כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן כַּחֲצוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the range and reasoning of the two views.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A triangle works for everyone. שמואל rejects a row because the ground between trees in a row can still be sown.

steps.title: רב המנונא challenges שמואל's reason with thorn bushes
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is only that one cannot sow between them, then buying three Roman thorn bushes should also give ground, which is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: According to the one who says a tripod, is the reason that one cannot sow between them? If so, if he sold him three Roman thorn bushes, which one cannot sow between, would he also own the ground?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא attacks the reason given for שמואל. He shows that it leads to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "no room to sow" were the whole reason, any three plants with no room between them would give the buyer ground. But thorn bushes are clearly not enough to give ownership of קרקע.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (now see where your logic leads)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna objected to this:
And according to the one who says like a tripod,
what is the reason – that one cannot sow between them?
But if so,
if he sold him three Roman thorn bushes,
which one cannot sow between,
would he also have the ground?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given for שמואל in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that a tripod works because one cannot sow between the trees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Then three thorn bushes, which also leave no room to sow, should give ownership of the ground, which is absurd.

steps.title: Thorn bushes are not significant; trees are
steps.stepSummary: Thorn bushes are not important enough to give ownership of ground. Trees are.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Those are not significant; these are significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to רב המנונא: no room to sow is not enough by itself. The plants must also be significant, like real trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things are needed: the plants must be significant, and (for שמואל) placed so the ground between them cannot be sown. Thorn bushes fail the first test, so the challenge falls away.
steps.whatToRemember: Buying three trees gives the buyer the ground between them. A cedar in the middle does not stop this. רב allows a row, שמואל requires a triangle. Only significant plants like trees count, not thorn bushes.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Those are not significant,
phrases.notes: "Those" are the thorn bushes; "these" in the next line are the trees.

phrases.english: these are significant.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any three plants with no room to sow between them would give ownership of the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only significant plants like trees give ownership of the ground; thorn bushes do not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The plants must be significant trees, not just plants that block sowing.

steps.title: Selling parts of a large animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that in a large animal (like a cow), selling one part does not include another: not head with legs, and not windpipe with liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sells the head of a large animal, he has not sold the legs. If he sells the legs, he has not sold the head. If he sells the windpipe, he has not sold the liver. If he sells the liver, he has not sold the windpipe.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that in a big animal, each part is sold on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a large animal, each part is big and valuable enough to count as its own item. So a sale of one part never pulls in a different part, in either direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text the גמרא will discuss)
A large domestic animal, like a cow or ox
Windpipe (here sold together with the lungs)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sells the head of a large animal
has not sold the legs;

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הָרַגְלַיִם – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הָרֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: if he sold the legs, he has not sold the head.

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַקָּנֶה – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַכָּבֵד,
phrases.english: If he sold the windpipe, he has not sold the liver;

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַכָּבֵד – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַקָּנֶה.
phrases.english: if he sold the liver, he has not sold the windpipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the trees-and-ground discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a large animal, selling the head, legs, windpipe, or liver does not include any other part.

steps.title: Selling parts of a small animal
steps.stepSummary: For a small animal, selling the head includes the legs, and selling the windpipe includes the liver. The reverse is not true.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a small animal: if he sells the head, he has sold the legs too, but if he sells the legs, he has not sold the head. If he sells the windpipe, he has sold the liver too, but if he sells the liver, he has not sold the windpipe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the large animal with a small animal (like a sheep or goat), where the rule works in only one direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a small animal, the legs and liver are minor next to the head and windpipe. So they come along with the main part. Selling only the minor part never brings in the main part.

keyTerms.meaning: A small domestic animal, like a sheep or goat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule simply flips for small animals. It works one way only: the main part (head, windpipe) brings along the lesser part, never the reverse.

phrases.english: But with a small animal:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הָרֹאשׁ – מָכַר אֶת הָרַגְלַיִם,
phrases.english: if he sold the head, he has sold the legs;

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הָרַגְלַיִם – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הָרֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: if he sold the legs, he has not sold the head.

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַקָּנֶה – מָכַר אֶת הַכָּבֵד,
phrases.english: If he sold the windpipe, he has sold the liver;

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַכָּבֵד – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַקָּנֶה.
phrases.english: if he sold the liver, he has not sold the windpipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts small animals with the large-animal rule of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a small animal, selling the head includes the legs and selling the windpipe includes the liver, but not the other way around.

steps.title: Four cases of wheat better or worse than promised
steps.stepSummary: If the wheat is worse than promised, the buyer may back out. If it is better, the seller may back out. If it matches what was said, nobody may back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are four cases with sellers. If he sold good wheat and it turned out bad, the buyer can back out. If he sold bad wheat and it turned out good, the seller can back out. If it was bad and turned out bad, or good and turned out good, neither one can back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new subject: backing out of a sale when the quality of the goods does not match what was said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the side that lost because of the mismatch may cancel. The buyer loses when he gets worse wheat, and the seller loses when he gives better wheat. When the wheat matches the description, the deal stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To back out of (cancel) the sale

phrases.english: There are four cases with sellers:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ חִטִּין יָפוֹת וְנִמְצְאוּ רָעוֹת –
phrases.english: if he sold him good wheat and it turned out bad,
the buyer can back out.
If it was sold as bad and turned out good,
the seller can back out.
Bad and it turned out bad;
good and it turned out good:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֶחָד מֵהֶם יָכוֹל לַחֲזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: neither one of them can back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה, about mistakes in a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the side that lost because of a quality mismatch may cancel. If there is no mismatch, the sale stands.

steps.title: A different kind of item: both may back out
steps.stepSummary: If the item turns out to be a different kind (another color of wheat, another wood, wine versus vinegar), both buyer and seller may back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sold reddish wheat and it turned out white, or white and it turned out reddish; olive wood and it turned out sycamore, or sycamore and it turned out olive; wine and it turned out vinegar, or vinegar and it turned out wine: both of them can back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a stronger case. Here the item is not just better or worse, but a different thing than what was agreed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wheat cases of step 13, only the side that lost may cancel. Here the item given is not the item that was sold at all. So the sale itself is flawed, and either side may cancel, even if no one lost money.
steps.whatToRemember: Better or worse quality: only the side that lost may cancel. A different kind of item: both sides may cancel.

phrases.english: Reddish-brown wheat that turned out white,
white that turned out reddish-brown;

phrases.aramaic: עֵצִים שֶׁל זַיִת וְנִמְצְאוּ שֶׁל שִׁקְמָה,
phrases.english: olive wood that turned out to be sycamore,
sycamore that turned out to be olive;
wine that turned out to be vinegar,
vinegar that turned out to be wine:
both of them can back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the four wheat cases with the case of a completely different item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the item turns out to be a different kind than agreed, both buyer and seller may cancel the sale.

steps.title: רב חסדא: overpaid, then the price went up
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that if the buyer paid six for something worth five, and it later rose to eight, only the buyer may back out, not the seller. He begins to give his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: if he sold him something worth five for six, and it became more expensive and rose to eight, who was cheated? The buyer. So the buyer can back out, and not the seller, because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ruling of רב חסדא about overcharging (אונאה) when prices change after the sale. His reason starts with 'because' and continues afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the time of the sale the buyer was the one who lost, since he overpaid. The later rise in price does not turn the seller into the cheated side. So the right to cancel belongs only to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The seller may feel that he is the loser now that the item is worth eight. But רב חסדא looks at who was cheated in the sale itself, and that was the buyer.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Ḥisda says:
if he sold him something worth five for six,
and it went up in price and stood at eight,
who was cheated? The buyer.

phrases.aramaic: לוֹקֵחַ יָכוֹל לַחֲזוֹר בּוֹ, וְלֹא מוֹכֵר;
phrases.english: So the buyer can back out, but not the seller;
because…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's rules about who may back out of a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the buyer overpaid and the price later rose, only the buyer may cancel, because he is the one who was cheated.
